subject: FUNCTION-ID paragraph
notes: §11.5.2 prints Format 1 `FUNCTION-ID. user-function-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] .` and Format 2 `FUNCTION-ID. function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] IS PROTOTYPE.` (IS not underlined => optional; FUNCTION-ID, AS, PROTOTYPE underlined; both periods required). cite.py --check 11.5.2 "Format 1 (definition)" OK; --check 11.5.2 "Format 2 (prototype)" OK. Grammar: `FUNCTION_ID DOT programName externalizedNamePhrase? prototypePhrase? DOT`, prototypePhrase = `IS? PROTOTYPE`, externalizedNamePhrase = `AS literal` (narrowed by ExternalizedName.Screen, the §11.5.3 SR1 row owned by landed PB303). Probes with the pinned cobol.exe (out/probe/fid): p1 Format 2 with AS + IS (`FUNCTION-ID. FIDPA AS "FIDREAL" IS PROTOTYPE.`) compiles+runs at 2002 and 2023 (P=000049); p2 Format 2 with IS omitted (`FUNCTION-ID. FIDPB PROTOTYPE.`) compiles+runs at 2002/2023; p4 missing period after FUNCTION-ID rejected (COBOL0307); p5 reversed order `IS PROTOTYPE AS "X"` rejected (COBOL0901 on AS — rejection correct, message names reservation rather than position); --std 85 rejects the prototype tail, the AS phrase and function reference with COBOL0900 (edition gate). Format 1 with/without AS is exercised by conformance:cases/8.3.2.2-User-defined-words/pb303_as_externalized_name and conformance:cases/_unassigned/udf_invocation; Format 2 without AS by conformance:cases/12.3.8-REPOSITORY/udf_prototype; NO existing golden covers Format 2 WITH AS literal-1 or the IS-omitted spelling, so test-ref is left empty (test-needed for those arms) rather than claiming whole-format coverage. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (FUNCTION-ID / user-defined functions and function prototypes are COBOL-2002 introductions; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to §11.5).
